title: unified-rollouts-canary-ab-shadow-autorollback-workflow
author: Jordan Lee
description: Context: customers need a single rollout primitive that supports canary, A/B, and shadow deployments with automatic rollback driven by configurable composite metrics. Motivation: reduce operational complexity and improve safety when promoting model versions across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. This PR implements a unified autorollback workflow that composes canary traffic, weighted A/B splits, and shadow probing into a single state machine with explicit safety guards and observability hooks. Summary of changes: adds a rollout controller state machine that tracks probes, canary windows, metric quorums, and quarantine stages; implements composite metric evaluator with configurable thresholds and quorum logic; introduces a shadow probing stage that runs requests through candidate models and computes divergence metrics without impacting production traffic; wires new rollout events into existing tracing and per-route telemetry; adds e2e tests and integration test harness updates. Key goals: 1) consistent behavior across canary/AB/shadow workflows, 2) deterministic automatic rollback when composite metrics fail, 3) improved telemetry for diagnosing rollout regressions. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-2384 - [x] State machine implementation with unit tests - [x] e2e test coverage for canary -> promote / canary -> rollback paths - [x] Observability: rollout spans, metric events, and dashboard panels - [x] Backwards-compatible config: rollout.policy defaults to previous behavior Migration notes: rollout.policy supports a new field "compositeMetrics" with a simple default so existing rollout configs keep their behavior. Customers that want auto-rollback must opt in by adding "autoRollback: true" to the rollout config or by using the new preset policies in the console. Testing notes: included unit tests for metric evaluation logic, integration tests that simulate traffic patterns and metric failures, and a small perf benchmark demonstrating negligible scheduling overhead (~1.2% at 1000rps). Security/operational notes: no changes to auth surface. The new workflow is gated behind a feature flag and will be rolled out to a subset of customers initially. Related work: builds on ENG-2401 (observability hooks) and SUP-9123 (customer incident follow-up).
